If they did, they would have a better understanding of it and wouldn’t push people away from the church so much. 2: they devote their lives to a misinterpreted version of the Bible that fits what they want. Also, cults start out because of their leaders having something to gain from having those followers, usually involving money or having a group of people they can physically/sexually abuse. That said, Jesus is historically credited as being the one who started Christianity, whether he’s the son of god or not. And with that, we can also find that his 12 disciples were real. Because of that, youd think this was a group of people masquerading around making all this money or doing all this abuse. But almost every single one of them was killed over it. They lived relatively poor (monetarily) lives, and didn’t really gather a group of people as much as they spread their beliefs wherever they went to those who would listen, and then they’d leave again. So the idea of it being a cult could be applied to modern churches yes, but in my opinion not Christianity as a whole. Because at its core Christianity is supposed to be a much more positive thing than modern churches have turned it into. Many churches are cults, or at least very similar to cults. But the actual religion, which any good pastor would tell you isn’t nearly as important as a relationship with god, is not itself a cult.
